sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic identification and source-level summary of the generalized strong Nyman-Beurling criterion, its necessity and compact-support sufficiency ranges.

sections_inspected.label: 1.1. Preliminaries and notation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the function spaces, fractional-part kernel, dilations and their spans, Mellin transform, and the dilation-invariant Muntz operator.

sections_inspected.label: 1.2. A generalized strong Nyman-Beurling theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recasts the strong criterion through the Muntz operator, motivates a family of kernels, defines good kernels, and states the necessary and sufficient implications with their limits.

sections_inspected.label: 2.1. Existence of P f
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Establishes almost-everywhere existence and local integrability of the Muntz transform using Burnol's integrability lemma and monotone convergence.

sections_inspected.label: 2.2. A convolution operator
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds a dilation-invariant integral operator, derives its weighted Lp norm bound from convolution on the multiplicative group, and factors a good kernel through it.

sections_inspected.label: 2.3. P as a convolution operator
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Represents the Muntz operator as pseudo-convolution against the fractional-part kernel, records mapping properties and endpoint failures, and proves the representation.

sections_inspected.label: 2.4. Muntz's formula
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Relates Mellin transformation of P f to multiplication by zeta, connects the general formula to the proto-Muntz identity, and proves it with an absolute-convergence check.

sections_inspected.label: 3.1. The necessity criterion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Explains the strategic surprise in the necessity direction and transports classical Nyman-Beurling approximants through a bounded dilation-invariant operator.

sections_inspected.label: 3.2. The sufficiency criterion
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Records the compact-support and prospective Lp boundaries, then uses a mean-cancelling dilation operator and bounded-support Mellin evaluation to force zeros of the kernel transform.

sections_inspected.label: References and author information
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliography and nonmathematical back matter, inspected for completeness but not segmented as source units.

accepted_units.title: Function spaces, dilation spans, and Mellin coordinates for the closure problem
accepted_units.why_material: Establishes the shared language in which the criterion is posed: vanishing and compactly supported function classes, the fractional-part kernel, bounded dilations K_lambda, the generated space B(g), and the Mellin transform analytic on the critical strip under the stated Lp hypothesis.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions are retained together because later closure, invariance, and zero-set claims depend simultaneously on these spaces and transforms; line 57 is incidental page furniture inside the span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Original PDF should be checked for C-space subscripts, rho_1, K_lambda, the Mellin hat, and the exact strip notation; the prose-supported roles are clear in the text layer.

accepted_units.title: The Muntz operator measures a sum-integral discrepancy and commutes with dilation
accepted_units.why_material: Defines P f as the difference between an extended sum of dilates and a scaled integral, then identifies dilation commutation as the structural property used to move generated spans through P and related operators.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the source's alternative Euler-difference/co-Poisson naming only where it clarifies the representation; existence is deliberately deferred to Section 2.1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula risk: verify equation (1.1), the position of 1/x, sum and integral limits, and K_lambda P=P K_lambda against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: The strong Nyman-Beurling criterion becomes a Muntz-generated closure problem
accepted_units.why_material: States the classical L2 closure equivalence, identifies direct Gramian computation as a stalled Hilbert-geometry route, uses P chi=-rho_1 to re-express the theorem, and formulates the search for kernels satisfying the analogous closure equivalence.
accepted_units.context_note: The obstruction and reformulation are kept with the theorem because the representation change is motivated precisely by the intractable scalar products of the original dilation family.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Original PDF required for L2-closure typography, scalar-product variables, equation (1.2), signs, and the exact logical direction of the displayed equivalences.

accepted_units.title: Strong kernels form a dilation-stable cone whose additive closure is unknown
accepted_units.why_material: Explores the generalized kernel family: step functions with zero-free Mellin transform provide examples, scalar multiplication and dilation preserve strength, addition is not known to do so, and this failure motivates restricting attention to a differentiable subspace with potentially tractable scalar products.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 98-103 intentionally overlap the generalized question in the preceding unit so that the term strong kernel and its target equivalence are locally intelligible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Verify the nonvanishing condition, exclusion of zero, Mellin-transform sum, and scalar-product integrals in the PDF; the cone-versus-subspace limitation is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Weighted derivative control forces decay and all-Lp integrability of good kernels
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the good-kernel class and proves from integration by parts that t f(t) tends to zero, ruling out a nonzero limiting constant by L1 integrability; this supplies the decay and integrability prerequisites used throughout the Muntz analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the forward reference that P f will lie in Lp for p>1 and vanish continuously at infinity, but does not treat that later result as already proved here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Original PDF required for the exact intersection of function spaces, weighted derivative integral, little-o statement, boundary term, and endpoint ranges.

accepted_units.title: Good kernels yield universal necessity but only compact-support sufficiency with a Mellin zero condition
accepted_units.why_material: States the paper's central asymmetry: RH sends every good kernel into the closure of dilates of P f, while compactly supported good kernels satisfying that closure can only force zeta zeros in the right half of the strip to be zeros of f-hat; a zero-free f-hat upgrades this to an equivalence.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the explicit wish to remove compact support so the theorem is not overread as a general biconditional for all good kernels.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High formula and logic risk: verify the definition of Z(g), implication nesting in (1.3)-(1.4), closure superscripts, compact-support class, and the zero-set inclusion in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Burnol's weighted sum bound makes the Muntz series well defined almost everywhere
accepted_units.why_material: Uses two monotone-convergence rearrangements and a counting-function bound to control the sum of |f(nx)| with dx/x, yielding almost-everywhere existence and local integrability of P f for good kernels.
accepted_units.context_note: The complete proof chain is retained because exchanging the infinite sum and integral is the actual certification mechanism, not routine algebra detachable from the conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the multi-line integral/sum chain, characteristic-function arguments, floor term, measures, and limits are spatially fragmented and must be verified against the PDF before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Multiplicative convolution imports Young's inequality and factors every good kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Defines the invariant operator T_F, proves its Lp norm bound by rewriting it as ordinary convolution on the multiplicative group with Haar measure dt/t, and records f=-T_{f'} chi, the identity later used to transfer Nyman-Beurling approximants.
accepted_units.context_note: The operator, norm theorem, factorization, and group change of variables form one mechanism: dilation invariance becomes translation-style convolution control after weighting.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: verify the T_F integral, weighted norm nu, exponents in phi and psi, Haar factors, the sign in f=-T_{f'}chi, and all p-dependent powers against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: P f is pseudo-convolution of f-prime with rho_1, with an Lp bound and a sharp endpoint warning
accepted_units.why_material: Gives an alternative definition P f=T_{f'}rho_1, derives Lp control for p>1, explains why P is not continuous in the ordinary Lp norm because the derivative remains exposed, and identifies rho_1 not in L1 as the endpoint obstruction.
accepted_units.context_note: The deferred continuity-at-infinity observation is retained as an explicitly unused property, not promoted into an established mechanism for the main theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: verify equation (2.5), argument order in rho_1(x/t), weighted norm index, p ranges, the value at the origin, and derivative notation in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Integration by parts and Burnol convergence identify the sum-integral operator with pseudo-convolution
accepted_units.why_material: Expands T_{f'}rho_1 through P chi, controls the integral term using t f(t) to zero, converts the indicator sum into truncated samples f(nx), invokes Burnol's lemma for absolute convergence, and recovers the defining sum-integral expression for P f.
accepted_units.context_note: The norm estimate at the end is included because it closes the representation proof by applying the preceding multiplicative-convolution bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high formula risk: equations (2.7)-(2.9), indicator arguments, truncation indices, floor bounds, signs, and limits require direct PDF verification; rely only on the checked prose for the proof architecture.

accepted_units.title: Muntz's formula turns P into multiplication by zeta under the Mellin transform
accepted_units.why_material: States the transform identity (P f)-hat=zeta times f-hat, shows that the nonsmooth characteristic kernel already realizes the proto-Muntz formula, and links this identity to the functional equation and Nyman-Beurling criteria before extending it to all good kernels.
accepted_units.context_note: Keeps the historical and scope remarks because they show that the same bridge supports both functional-equation proofs and closure criteria while admitting still more general formulations elsewhere.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: verify the hats, sign and factor -s in (2.11), strip bounds, smoothness/decay hypotheses, and exact equation (2.10) against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Pseudo-convolution factorization proves Muntz's formula with an explicit Fubini certificate
accepted_units.why_material: Substitutes P f=T_{f'}rho_1 into the Mellin integral, separates variables using the proto-Muntz identity, integrates by parts to obtain f-hat, and repeats the calculation with absolute values to justify the interchange for every point in the critical strip.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 367-368 overlap the theorem statement so the proof's hypotheses are present; the absolute-integrability tail is essential certification rather than disposable calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: all iterated integrals, substitutions, powers, zeta factors and signs in lines 376-420 are visually split; formula-level extraction must use the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: The necessity route tests RH without requiring a nonvanishing kernel Mellin transform
accepted_units.why_material: The author frames the generalized necessity condition as a possible disproof test using analytically tractable kernels and stresses that, unlike the earlier proof for chi, it requires no Mellin-transform condition on the chosen kernel.
accepted_units.context_note: This is source-grounded strategic interpretation and contrast, not evidence that such a tractable kernel or RH disproof has been found.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose is clear; verify only the exact chi-hat formula and theorem reference in the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A bounded dilation-invariant operator transports classical approximants to every good kernel
accepted_units.why_material: Starts from RH-conditioned approximants to -chi in B(rho_1), applies T_{f'} to them, uses commutation with dilations and P f=T_{f'}rho_1 to land in B(P f), and uses f=-T_{f'}chi plus L2 boundedness to preserve convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the complete necessity mechanism and leaves visible its dependence on the already established strong Nyman-Beurling theorem and on f being a good kernel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: verify coefficient indices, signs in h_n+chi and H_n-f, closure notation, and the exact T_{f'} and K_a compositions in equations (3.1)-(3.2).

accepted_units.title: Compact support blocks analytic kernels, while the expected Lp extension lacks matching necessity theory
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies removal of compact support as the immediate open improvement needed to admit analytically promising kernels, and records the expected Lp half-plane analogue together with the precise reason it is not claimed: neither necessity direction has been worked out in that setting.
accepted_units.context_note: The expected Lp result is explicitly a prospective generalization, not a theorem of the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: PDF check advisable for the half-plane threshold Re(s)>1/p and the exact Lp qualifiers; the scope limitation is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Mean cancellation and compact support convert L2 closure into pointwise Mellin vanishing
accepted_units.why_material: At a zeta zero in the right half of the strip, applies V=I-2K_2 to the approximating family, creating a compactly supported mean-zero F whose P F and generated approximants vanish beyond a common bound; Muntz's formula kills their Mellin values, and Cauchy-Schwarz on the bounded interval passes the zero to F-hat and hence f-hat.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit retains every condition needed for the argument: compact support, mean zero, the fixed zero range, L2 convergence, common bounded support, and square-integrability of x^(s-1) only on that bounded interval.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Very high: verify V, the integral-zero statement, common-support claim, Mellin hats, signs, Schwarz exponent condition, and the factor (1-2^(1-s)) in the original PDF; the extracted line 486 compresses the exponent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The generalized criterion is transported rather than reproved kernel by kernel
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The original pair chi and -rho_1 is sent by the bounded dilation-intertwining operator T_{f'} to the pair -f and P f, so RH-conditioned closure approximants transfer functorially to every good kernel instead of requiring a new Gramian calculation for each one.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This proves only the RH-to-closure necessity direction, depends on the established strong Nyman-Beurling theorem and good-kernel regularity, and does not make the resulting scalar products computable.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: P has complementary physical-space and Mellin-space representations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same operator is certified as an almost-everywhere sum-integral discrepancy, represented as dilation convolution against rho_1, and diagonalized by the Mellin transform as multiplication by zeta; the existence, norm, and Fubini arguments connect these views rather than treating them as formal identities.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The bridge is proved only under the source's good-kernel/integrability hypotheses, fails at the stated L1 endpoint, exposes derivatives in physical-space continuity, and its exact formulas require PDF verification.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Sufficiency relocates the problem to zeros of the kernel Mellin transform
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Closure of f by dilates of P f, after mean cancellation and compactification, forces every zeta zero in the right half of the critical strip to be a zero of f-hat; choosing a compactly supported good kernel with zero-free Mellin transform would therefore turn this inclusion into an RH equivalence.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not remove compact support, construct a new tractable zero-free analytic kernel, or prove the expected Lp analogue; the criterion relocates these obligations rather than solving them.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The paper replaces direct Hilbert geometry with invariant-operator geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The stalled route asks for explicit Gramian distances among fractional-part dilates, whereas the generalized necessity proof uses a bounded operator commuting with every dilation to preserve approximation abstractly and opens a search over kernels whose scalar products might be simpler.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The broader kernel family is only cone-like, additive closure remains unknown, and no kernel with demonstrably decisive scalar-product geometry is produced in this note.
